LESSON: MAKING CHOICES

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Creation
Topic 1.3: Making choices

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Making choices. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are the effects of the choices you make?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. discuss results of choices they make in daily life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MAKING CHOICES
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Making choices helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: MAKING CHOICES
Study Making choices like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Discuss results of choices they make in daily life

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss results of choices they make in daily life. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss results of choices they make in daily life.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Making choices” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss results of choices they make in daily life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Making choices is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Making choices” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: discuss results of choices they make in daily life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Making choices to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: discuss results of choices they make in daily life.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Making choices from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Making choices: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Making choices?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the effects of the choices you make?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Making choices means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: discuss results of choices they make in daily life.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
